name: Nailted
tagline: Employee engagement platform that runs recurring anonymous pulse surveys, eNPS and 1:1 prompts, mostly delivered through Slack or Teams.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanical core here is a cron job, a question bank, a Slack message and a bar chart, and an agent will give you that in a weekend. What you cannot build in a weekend is the part that makes engagement surveys worth anything: cross-company benchmarks, a question set that has been tuned against real response data, and employees who actually believe the answers are anonymous. A self-hosted version is fine for a founder who wants a temperature check on twelve people and does not care about percentile scoring. It stops being fine the moment HR needs to defend a number to a board, or an employee asks who can read the database. Build it for a small team, buy it if the survey results are going into someone's performance conversation.
coreLoopDIY: Schedules recurring pulse surveys to Slack on a rotating question set, collects responses behind one-time anonymous tokens, and renders score trends and eNPS on a simple dashboard.
requirements: A Slack workspace and a bot token with chat:write and users:read
A small always-on host for the scheduler (a VPS or a free tier container)
Someone willing to be the person who technically has database access
A real question set, which is the part you will underestimate
whatYouLose: Cross-industry benchmarks, so your 7.4 engagement score means nothing in isolation
Credible anonymity: self-hosted means a colleague owns the box, and people will assume the worst
A validated question library and the survey cadence logic that keeps response rates up
Manager-level reporting, team slicing and permission boundaries between who sees what
HRIS sync, so org structure and leavers are maintained by hand
moatNotes: The benchmark corpus and the perception of anonymity are the product. The survey delivery is plumbing.
whyPeopleStillPay: Engagement data is only useful if people answer honestly and if the resulting number can be compared to something. A third party solves both at once: employees trust an external platform more than an internal database, and the vendor can tell you whether your eNPS is bad or just normal for a 40 person startup in your sector. Add HR leaders who need a defensible process rather than a homegrown script, plus HRIS and SSO integrations that make the thing survive headcount changes, and the subscription keeps renewing even though the underlying app is simple.
notes: Easy to clone, hard to be believed. The benchmarks and the anonymity are doing the real work.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted employee pulse survey tool. Stack: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind for styling, Recharts for charts. No external services beyond Slack.

Data model:
- employees: id, slack_user_id, display_name, team, active
- questions: id, text, dimension (one of: workload, management, growth, belonging, enps), scale (1-10 or 0-10 for enps)
- cycles: id, opened_at, closed_at, question_ids (json)
- invites: id, cycle_id, employee_id, token (random 32 chars), used_at
- responses: id, cycle_id, question_id, score, comment, created_at  -- deliberately NO employee_id, do not add one

Behaviour:
1. A scheduler (node-cron inside a small worker script) opens a new cycle every two weeks: pick 4 rotating questions plus the eNPS question every third cycle.
2. For each active employee, create an invite with a single-use token and DM them a Slack link to /survey/[token] using chat.postMessage.
3. /survey/[token] renders the questions with 1-10 buttons and one optional free-text comment. On submit, write rows to responses with no identity link and mark the invite used. Reject used or unknown tokens.
4. /dashboard shows: response rate per cycle, average score per dimension over time as a line chart, eNPS computed as promoters minus detractors, and a list of comments in random order. Suppress all output for any cycle with fewer than 5 responses and show "not enough responses" instead.
5. Seed 18 reasonable pulse questions across the dimensions in a seed script.

Explicitly out of scope: SSO, HRIS sync, per-manager permissions, benchmarks against other companies, email delivery, mobile app, multi-tenant anything.

Secrets: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN and APP_BASE_URL in .env, loaded with dotenv, .env in .gitignore. No telemetry, no analytics scripts.

Ship: a README with setup steps, npm run seed, npm run dev, npm run worker, and a one-paragraph honest note in the README explaining that anonymity here is a promise about the code and not a technical guarantee, since whoever runs the server can read the database.
